title: Invoice line-item suppression during batched rollup after node eviction
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: A large Dedicated customer reported that their monthly invoice omitted several line items for burst streaming tokens on 2026-02-17. Automated billing alerts also detected a sharp drop in expected rolling-rollup token counts for the customer's tenant during the same window. The underlying condition appears when a Dedicated node is evicted during autoscaling while an in-progress batched rollup job is aggregating per-tenant token events. The rollup coordinator's 'suppress-if-duplicate' logic mistakenly considered partially-committed shard windows fully applied when the eviction triggered a replay from the node's local KV cache. This resulted in suppression of the final line items instead of producing corrected rollup entries.

Impact: High — customer-facing invoice undercounts leading to manual credits and loss of trust. Affected tenants: 1 enterprise customer (reported) plus an estimated 3 additional tenants with similar traffic patterns across Dedicated pools in us-west-2 between 2026-02-17T02:00-02:30 UTC. Short-term revenue delta is material and requires backfill and customer credits.

Hypothesis / Root cause: The rollup job uses event identity based on (shard_id, window_start, event_hash). When a node eviction occurs mid-window, a restarted worker replays buffered events with identical event_hash but missing a final 'commit' marker. The suppress-if-duplicate code treats identical hashes as already-applied if a commit marker exists elsewhere; in this scenario, the commit did not persist to the canonical ledger due to a race with eviction and local checkpointing behavior. Consequently, the ledger state and emitted invoice lines were inconsistent: ledger showed low totals and the billing export suppressed emission for those windows.

Repro steps:
1. Provision a Dedicated pool and configure a high-throughput tenant with continuous streaming requests.
2. Force an eviction (simulate preemption or scale-down) while the rollup job is aggregating a window.
3. Observe that replayed events with same hashes are replayed by restarting worker; the final commit fails to persist due to transient write timeout.
4. Run billing-export; verify missing line items for the window.

Mitigation (short-term):
- Manual backfill: run the rollup reconcilier to rehydrate suppressed line items and re-run billing export for affected tenants (runbook: https://confluence.company/internal/metering/backfill-runbook).
- Customer-facing mitigation: issue temporary credits and provide a transparent incident summary; enable conservative billing mode (emit provisional line items rather than suppress) for affected Dedicated pools.

Fix (long-term):
- Change rollup idempotency to include a monotonic event_sequence per shard plus explicit commit checkpoints persisted before suppression logic can apply.
- Make the suppress-if-duplicate logic require both matching event_hash and persisted commit marker in canonical ledger (rather than local KV acknowledgements).
- Add a reconciler that runs after node eviction to detect suppressed windows and re-enqueue them for rollup (implementation PR linked below).

Work in progress:
- hotfix branch: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/compare/hotfix/rollup-eviction-2026 (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/4289) — hotfix changes suppress behavior to be conservative and adds a one-off reconciler script.
- Instrumentation dashboards: billing-rollup-lag (Grafana) + billing-export-drop-rates (Datadog) updated to show suppressed-windows metric.

Next steps / owner actions:
- Marcus Li: finish and land hotfix PR, deploy to us-west-2 dedicated staging, validate with synthetic eviction tests (ETA 2026-03-08).
- Aisha Patel: run manual backfill for affected tenants and prepare customer remediation package (ETA 2026-03-07).
- SRE: schedule immediate run of reconciler on affected clusters and monitor for additional suppressed windows.

Related artifacts: incident ticket CS-11234 (customer escalation), runbook link above, PR 4289, internal postmortem draft: https://drive.company/internal/postmortems/2026-02-billing-suppression-draft
